blocks.text: How selling works, step by step

parts.t: 1. First chat
We talk about why you're moving, your timeline and what you need from the sale. I explain how I work and the B.C. disclosure forms you'll sign. This is free.
2. Pricing
I compare your home with recent sales and current listings close by. You get a price range and the reasons behind it.
Start with a free home evaluation
3. Getting ready
We pick the few jobs worth doing, such as cleaning, small repairs and clearing clutter. You don't need to renovate. Staging help comes with every listing.
4. Photos and listing
Every listing gets professional photos, video, floor plans and drone photos. Then your home goes on the MLS® and my website. See my
marketing plan
5. Showings
Buyers book through their agents. I share feedback with you after each one so you know what people think.
6. Offers
I walk you through each offer: price, deposit, conditions and dates. We decide together whether to accept, counter or wait.
7. Conditions and cooling-off
Most buyers have conditions such as financing or an inspection. For most homes, buyers also get a three business day cooling-off period after acceptance.
8. Closing
Your lawyer or notary handles the paperwork and pays out your mortgage. You hand over the keys on possession day.

blocks.text: What it costs to sell a home in B.C.

parts.t: These are common costs when you sell, from the BC Financial Services Authority (BCFSA) list:

items.t: Legal or notary fees for the title transfer
Legal fees to discharge your mortgage

parts.t: Any prepayment penalty from your lender for paying the mortgage off early
Your share of the current year's property taxes, if not already paid

If you sell a home you've owned for less than 730 days, the BC home flipping tax may apply. The rate is 20% of the profit for homes sold within 365 days, and it drops to zero by day 730. Some exemptions apply, and a return may be due within 90 days of the sale.
If a buyer cancels during the three business day cooling-off period, they pay you a fee of 0.25% of the offer price.
For tax questions about your own sale, talk to an accountant.

What costs come with selling a home in B.C.?
Common costs include legal or notary fees, the fee to discharge your mortgage, GST on legal fees, any mortgage prepayment penalty and your share of property taxes. BCFSA lists these on its
selling costs page
How do you decide my list price?
I look at what similar homes near you sold for recently, what is listed now and what makes your home different. You get a price range with the reasons. Start with a
free home evaluation
Can a buyer back out after I accept their offer?
For most homes in B.C., a buyer can cancel within three business days after you accept. They must tell you in writing and pay you 0.25% of the offer price. See the
BCFSA rules
Do I pay tax if I sell soon after buying?
The BC home flipping tax may apply if you owned the home for less than 730 days. Some exemptions apply. See the
Government of B.C. page
and talk to an accountant.
Do I need to renovate before selling?
Usually not. Cleaning, small repairs and clearing clutter often matter more. I'll tell you which jobs are worth doing, and staging help comes with every listing.
How long does it take to sell?
It depends on your home, price and the market at the time. I'll show you how long similar homes near you have taken to sell recently.
